articles.summary: Medical device manufacturer Medtronic has confirmed a data breach following claims by hackers that they stole 9 million records from the company's corporate IT systems.

articles.title: Chinese spy posed as researcher in spear-phishing campaign targeting NASA to steal defense software
articles.summary: A Chinese national conducted a spear-phishing campaign by impersonating a U.S. researcher to deceive NASA employees into divulging sensitive defense software and export data.

articles.title: LINKEDIN BROWSERGATE
articles.summary: An investigation by Fairlinked, dubbed 'BrowserGate', alleges that LinkedIn is secretly fingerprinting users through browser extensions and device data to share information with third parties for tracking. The report characterizes these practices as a significant data privacy scandal involving unauthorized data collection.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Fast16 Malware, XChat Launch, Federal Backdoor, AI Employee Tracking & More
articles.summary: The weekly recap highlights a return of legacy cyber threats and credential-based attacks, emphasizing the persistent risk of supply chain vulnerabilities and abused remote tools. It underscores that many of these systemic security failures stem from long-standing, unresolved issues.

articles.title: Hackers impersonate Microsoft Teams help desk to breach corporate networks
articles.summary: Threat actors are masquerading as Microsoft Teams support personnel to deceive users into installing malicious software designed to exfiltrate corporate data. This social engineering tactic poses a significant risk to organizational network security.

articles.title: Trump's Golden Dome gets $3.2BN of contractors and an AI sprinkle
articles.summary: The U.S. government has awarded $3.2 billion in contracts to upgrade missile defense systems, with a significant emphasis on integrating artificial intelligence capabilities.

articles.title: Money launderer linked to $230M crypto heist gets 70 months in prison
articles.summary: A 22-year-old California man, Evan Tangeman, was sentenced to 70 months in prison for his role in laundering funds stolen during a $230 million cryptocurrency heist.

articles.title: Deepfake Voice Attacks are Outpacing Defenses: What Security Leaders Should Know
articles.summary: Deepfake voice technology now requires only three seconds of audio to facilitate fraudulent activities, effectively bypassing many current security measures. This trend poses a significant risk to organizations as attackers increasingly use manipulated calls to deceive employees into conducting unauthorized financial transactions.

articles.title: Cybersec is a thankless job: expanding workload and shrinking pay packet
articles.summary: Cybersecurity professionals are facing increasing job dissatisfaction due to growing workloads paired with stagnating or declining compensation. This trend highlights a significant retention challenge within the industry.

articles.title: UNC6692 Hackers Exploit Microsoft Teams to Deploy SNOW Malware
articles.summary: The threat actor group UNC6692 is actively using deceptive Microsoft Teams IT alerts to distribute SNOW malware and compromise corporate networks. This campaign focuses on credential theft and unauthorized access through social engineering tactics.

articles.title: Mythos Changed the Math on Vulnerability Discovery. Most Teams Aren't Ready for the Remediation Side
articles.summary: The introduction of Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI for large-scale vulnerability discovery has triggered concerns regarding the operational capacity of security teams to effectively validate and remediate the influx of findings. This shift highlights a growing disconnect between automated detection capabilities and existing organizational response workflows.

articles.title: PhantomCore Exploits TrueConf Vulnerabilities to Breach Russian Networks
articles.summary: The pro-Ukrainian hacktivist group PhantomCore is exploiting an exploit chain of three vulnerabilities in TrueConf video conferencing software to remotely execute commands on Russian networks. The campaign, which began in September 2025, was detailed in a report by Positive Technologies.

articles.title: Burglar alarm biz burgled: ADT confirms cyber intrusion after ShinyHunters extortion attempt
articles.summary: ADT has confirmed a cyber intrusion following an extortion attempt by the threat actor group ShinyHunters. The incident involved unauthorized access to the company's systems, leading to a formal security investigation.

articles.title: Researchers Uncover 73 Fake VS Code Extensions Delivering GlassWorm v2 Malware
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified 73 malicious or cloned Visual Studio Code extensions on the Open VSX registry used to distribute the GlassWorm v2 information-stealing malware. The campaign targets developers by mimicking legitimate extensions to facilitate persistent unauthorized access and data theft.

articles.title: Microsoft updates the Windows Update Experience: You can hit pause now
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced a new feature to the Windows Update process that allows users to manually pause updates, offering greater control over their system's maintenance schedule. This update aims to provide more flexibility to users who previously had limited options for deferring installation.

articles.title: Firefox bug CVE-2026-6770 enabled cross-site tracking and Tor fingerprinting
articles.summary: CVE-2026-6770 is a vulnerability in Firefox and Tor Browser that allowed attackers to track and fingerprint users, even while using Private Browsing or the New Identity feature. The issue has been addressed in Firefox 150 and Tor Browser 15.0.10.

articles.title: Vidar Infostealer Spreads via Fake CAPTCHAs, Hides in JPEG and TXT Files
articles.summary: A new iteration of the Vidar infostealer is being distributed through deceptive CAPTCHA prompts, utilizing steganography to conceal malicious payloads within image and text files. The malware executes fileless attacks to exfiltrate sensitive user information, including browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data.

articles.title: ICO chief John Edwards steps back as workplace probe quietly unfolds
articles.summary: The UK Information Commissioner, John Edwards, has temporarily stepped back from his role while an internal workplace investigation is conducted. The investigation's specific details remain undisclosed.

articles.title: Fast16: Pre-Stuxnet malware that targeted precision engineering software
articles.summary: SentinelOne has identified Fast16, a sophisticated 2005-era sabotage malware that manipulated precision engineering software and predates the Stuxnet worm. The discovery reveals early state-sponsored cyber operations that utilized Lua-based code to disrupt industrial calculation integrity.

articles.title: Anthropic's magic code-sniffer: More Swiss cheese than cheddar, for now
articles.summary: Anthropic's new code-scanning tool is currently demonstrating significant security deficiencies and reliability issues, leaving it vulnerable to potential bypasses. The headline implies the tool is currently ineffective at providing robust protection for codebases.

articles.title: Italy moves to extradite Chinese national to the U.S. over hacking charges
articles.summary: Italy has initiated the extradition process for Chinese national Xu Zewei, who is wanted by U.S. authorities for alleged cyber-espionage and hacking of COVID-19 research linked to state-backed operations.

articles.title: U.S. utility giant Itron discloses a security breach
articles.summary: U.S. utility company Itron has initiated its incident response protocol after discovering unauthorized access to its internal IT systems on April 13, 2026. The company is currently working with external security experts and has notified relevant authorities regarding the breach.

articles.title: Fake CAPTCHA IRSF Scam and 120 Keitaro Campaigns Drive Global SMS, Crypto Fraud
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging fake CAPTCHA prompts and Keitaro traffic distribution systems to trick users into sending unauthorized, premium-rate international SMS messages. This global fraud campaign generates illicit revenue by exploiting mobile billing systems.

articles.title: Google Cloud Next proves what we suspected: Everything is AI now
articles.summary: Service busy.

articles.title: Microsoft Entra Agent ID Flaw Enabled Tenant Takeover via Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: Service busy.

articles.title: Critical bug in CrowdStrike LogScale let attackers access files
articles.summary: CrowdStrike has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-40050) in its self-hosted LogScale product that could allow unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server. Security updates have been released to address the flaw.

articles.title: American utility firm Itron discloses breach of internal IT network
articles.summary: American utility company Itron, Inc. has reported a cybersecurity breach involving unauthorized access to its internal IT network via an SEC 8-K filing. The company is currently investigating the incident to determine the scope of the impact.

articles.title: GopherWhisper: new China-linked APT targets Mongolia with Go-based malware
articles.summary: A China-linked APT group identified as GopherWhisper is targeting Mongolian government institutions using a sophisticated suite of Go-based loaders and backdoors. ESET researchers discovered this campaign, highlighting the group's focus on regional espionage.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 94
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware threats, including the Morpheus spyware, DarkSword and Coruna exploits targeting iPhones, and the Lotus Wiper targeting energy infrastructure. It provides a curated overview of critical cybersecurity research and emerging malicious activity.

articles.title: Trigona ransomware adopts custom tool to steal data and evade detection
articles.summary: Trigona ransomware has transitioned to a custom-built data exfiltration tool to improve efficiency and bypass security detection mechanisms previously triggered by standard utilities like Rclone. This shift reflects an evolving tactical approach aimed at gaining greater control over stolen data and evading discovery.

articles.title: Hot take: AI's not going to kill open source code security
articles.summary: The article argues against the prevailing sentiment that artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to the security of open-source software. It suggests that AI will likely serve as a tool to enhance rather than compromise secure development practices.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 574 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The Security Affairs newsletter highlights CISA's addition of critical vulnerabilities in SimpleHelp, Samsung, and D-Link products to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
